title: OutSystems Screen Inventory (shared artifact for N outsystems-ui-design runs)

x_downstream_contract.note: app_chrome, assertions and archetype are borrowed vocabulary, not new ones. app_chrome.layout_block/app_title/menu are the exact fields outsystems-ui-design's cross-blueprint chrome pass compares; assertions accepts only the links/buttons/inputs vocabulary shared with that validator and outsystems-mentor-implementation/scripts/recompute_assertions.py; archetype is one of the 14 archetypes outsystems-ui-design confirms at Step 1. Changing any of them here without changing them there breaks the loop.
x_downstream_contract.authority: scripts/validate_screen_inventory.py is the enforced contract; this schema documents it.

design_tokens_source.description: OPTIONAL. Where the design runs read visual identity (colors, typography) from — an approved sibling blueprint, an as-built theme. Greenfield trial G-05: the brief carried no tokens and the design run mined a sibling blueprint on its own; when a source exists, record it so --brief hands it over. When absent, the brief derives a default from source.kind (modernization: the as-built theme; requirements-doc: states there is no source yet).

kind.description: Where the candidates came from. 'requirements-doc': a PRD/brief, candidates are the screen-worthy capabilities it names. 'existing-app-modernization': a live app, candidates are its existing screens.

refs.description: Paths or citations for the source document(s). An inventory with no traceable source cannot be audited against its requirements.

app_chrome.description: The one chrome decision, made up front and copied verbatim into every blueprint. Deciding it per screen is what the cross-blueprint chrome pass exists to catch.

target.description: Must name a screen in screens[].

menu.description: Menu entries IN ORDER. Order is compared across blueprints downstream; `active` is deliberately not carried here because each screen highlights its own entry. When the app's copy is localized, `label` is the half that is translated; `target` is the stable screen identity plan traceability and blueprints resolve against and is never translated.

candidates.description: Every screen-worthy thing the source named, before fusion. No candidate is silently dropped: each one resolves to at least one screen, is explicitly dissolved into something that is not a screen, or is explicitly excluded from this build with a stated reason.

source_ref.description: Where in the source this candidate came from. When source.kind is 'requirements-doc' this MUST name at least one requirement ID the source defines, in the grammar outsystems-plan-to-mentor owns (BR-/UC-/C-, optionally with a scope infix), with free prose as a trailing note: 'BR-SC-002 - the room list section'. Without the ID the requirement-to-screen binding exists only as prose here and gets invented a second time in the capability plan's Traceability table. For 'existing-app-modernization' the check does not apply: candidates trace to an existing app's screens and there is no ID grammar to cite.

disposition.description: In scope — 'mapped': at least one screen absorbs it; 'dissolved': not a destination, but the capability lives somewhere else in this build (say where, in dissolved_into). Excluded — 'deferred' (a later build takes it), 'out-of-scope' (it belongs to another product), 'accepted-risk' (a known gap nobody owns): the candidate is not in this build at all. These three are borrowed verbatim from outsystems-plan-to-mentor's closed requirement-disposition vocabulary so an excluded id keeps its meaning downstream. An excluded candidate carries neither resolves_to nor dissolved_into, states its reason in rationale, and is rendered by --brief as a do-NOT-implement line so the exclusion survives the handoff instead of dying here.

resolves_to.description: Screens that absorb this candidate. More than one is legitimate — a candidate can split across screens (the reference half of a page becoming onboarding, the console half becoming an operation).

dissolved_into.description: Required when dissolved: where the capability lives now. It was never a destination, but it still has to exist somewhere.

non_screen_requirements.description: OPTIONAL. Requirements the source defines that produce no screen — a hashing rule, a retention policy, a background job. Listing one here is how the --source absorption check distinguishes a deliberate non-screen decision from an oversight; without this slot, silence would be the only way to say either. Acceptance criteria (C- rows) belong here as a normal, expected category and often in bulk: a criterion states how a screen is verified, not that one exists. Give each the same one-line reason - `acceptance criterion - verified against <screen>, produces no screen`. An ID listed here must not also be cited as a candidate's provenance.

id.description: A requirement ID in the same grammar as candidates[].source_ref (BR-/UC-/C- with an optional scope infix). It must be defined in the --source document when one is supplied.

reason.description: Why this requirement produces no screen. A bare exclusion list is indistinguishable from an oversight.

presentation_pattern.description: OPTIONAL refinement of archetype: the ODC presentation block this screen's main collection is laid out in, named in outsystems-ui-design's own block vocabulary (references/blocks-index.md). Taking it here takes the list-vs-gallery-vs-cards decision ONCE, for the whole app, instead of N design runs each re-taking it from the same requirements. A design run reads it from --brief as a HINT: it may diverge, but not silently - a divergence is a design decision it has to state. Absent is the normal answer wherever the screen lays out no collection (edit-form, wizard, settings, instructional), and a plain non-card list (IList + ListItemContent) has no value here on purpose - omit rather than approximate.

behavior.description: What the screen DOES. Trial F-11: an inventory of names alone left block choices and interactions to be reconciled by hand.

behavior_notes.description: Behavioural contract of the binding — caps, limits, states, async semantics. Trial F-11: a 10-row cap on the action a whole screen read through sat one field away from what the inventory captured.

introduced_here.description: True when this inventory is where the name was born (greenfield trial G-05). Entities only — a new action's name is born in the capability plan, never here (the no-logic-design scope guard; method R8's greenfield asymmetry). The --brief output prints a delegation line for these: names are authoritative, attribute shapes are the capability plan's to type, and a design run must not invent them.

accepts.description: Payload names this screen can receive from another screen. A navigation edge carrying a payload must find it here (trial F-12).

assertions.description: OPTIONAL and restricted to the shared vocabulary. Declare a count only when the requirement itself pins it; this is a carry-forward seed for the blueprint, not a design decision made at inventory time.

entry_point.description: True when users land on this screen from outside the app's own navigation (deep link, external URL, notification). Such a screen is a reachability root alongside the menu targets; without it, a screen no menu entry or navigation path reaches is an error.

access_classification.description: OPTIONAL. Who this screen is FOR, declared as intent so a later run can reconcile the built app against it rather than re-deriving it from the model. The writer default is never the policy: a screen nobody decided is 'unresolved', not 'public'. 'unresolved' blocks the screen from being built - stop and ask. 'preview_public' is a build-time convenience that must never survive to promotion. Reconciliation keys on the built screen's anonymousAccess plus roles[], never on a Public:true flag.

access_role.description: Required when access_classification is 'role': the role name that gates this screen. The role's existence is a PRECONDITION - verify it exists before the screen is created, not after. Validation checks only that a role screen names a role; it cannot check that the role exists, because this artifact is authored with no tenant to ask. A named role is a claim to verify, not a verified fact.

record_actions.description: OPTIONAL. Where this screen's create / edit / detail on a record actually happens. A list screen that offers CREATE or EDIT and says nowhere it happens is warned, and blocked at --handoff: two apps shipped 'add' and per-row 'edit' controls whose destination screens were in nobody's inventory, so the controls were built, rendered, and did nothing. Declaring is the only way to settle it, because prose does not: on the app that paid for this rule the behavior field asserted the mutation happened on the screen while the build produced navigation controls to screens that did not exist. 'detail' is declarable and a declared one is held to its rules, but an undeclared row-open is never warned about - it is the commonest edge in any list app, its trigger names the gesture rather than the verb ('select an item row'), and inferring it accused screens whose row-open was already correctly closed. A declared entry is held to its rules; an inventory written before the field existed is untouched.

action.description: The record action this entry answers for. Each may be declared at most once per screen.

resolves_to.description: One of three answers: the name of the screen this action opens (which must be a screen in this inventory AND the target of a navigation edge from this one, because a control that opens a screen IS an edge and the edge is what carries the trigger and the payload); the literal 'inline' when it happens on this screen; or the literal 'out-of-scope' when the action is not in this build - in which case the control must NOT be built, and no key interaction may still offer it, because a screen that describes an action while declaring its control unbuilt has said both things at once.

reason.description: Required when resolves_to is 'out-of-scope'. An unexplained one is a capability deleted silently.

open_decisions.description: OPTIONAL. Decisions this inventory has NOT taken, as typed data rather than prose. Hard gate 5's autonomous-run disclosure previously instructed the model to name its least-confident fusion in chat, which the artifact does not carry; this is the slot that does. Each entry is a real choice: 2-4 options, each naming exactly what this inventory would say if that option were taken. An open decision never fails validation - it marks the inventory PROPOSED, NOT APPROVED in the validation report and rides the per-screen --brief so a design run cannot settle it unknowingly.

about.description: The decision itself, stated so a reviewer can take it without reconstructing it.

category.description: Deliberately this skill's own scope and nothing wider: candidate-disposition (hard gate 2 - is this candidate a screen at all), screen-fusion (hard gate 5 - are these one screen or two), chrome (hard gate 3), navigation (R7), binding (R6/R8 - which entity or action, by name). A decision about block choice, visual design or logic belongs to outsystems-ui-design or the capability plan; recording it here would create a second declaration site neither of them reads.

options.description: One option is a position and five is a survey; neither is a decision a reviewer can take in one pass.

consequence.description: Exactly what this inventory would say if this option were taken - the screen that appears or disappears, the menu entry gained or lost, the binding that changes. A label alone is the prose the typed slot exists to replace.

resolution.description: Required when resolved, and forbidden while open: the id of the option taken. A resolved decision with no resolution records that someone decided and not what they decided.

affects.description: OPTIONAL. Screen names this decision bears on; each must name a screen in screens[]. Omit it when the decision is app-wide (chrome, most navigation) - an unscoped decision reaches EVERY screen's brief, so the decisions with the widest blast radius are not the silent ones.

payload.description: What is handed to the target screen. The target must list it in `accepts`.
